analysis.evidence: The plural verb agrees with יְמֵי אָדָם, “Adam’s days.” אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת שֵׁת marks the period after he fathered Seth, and שְׁמֹנֶה מֵאֹת שָׁנָה gives its length as eight hundred years.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person masculine plural, with prefixed conjunction וַ־.
analysis.sense: to amount to a stated duration

analysis.evidence: יְמֵי אָדָם means “the days of Adam.” אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת שֵׁת limits the phrase to the part of Adam’s life after he fathered Seth, a span the verse measures as eight hundred years.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural noun in the construct state, with אָדָם as its complement.
analysis.sense: (pl.) days of a life, a reign or an age

analysis.evidence: In יְמֵי אָדָם, “the days of Adam,” the name identifies whose years are counted. אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת שֵׁת, “after he fathered Seth,” identifies Adam as a specific father in the genealogy.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun in the absolute state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אַחֲרֵי introduces הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת שֵׁת, “he fathered Seth.” The verse counts the eight hundred years Adam lived after that event.
analysis.morphology: Preposition in the plural construct form אַחֲרֵי, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת שֵׁת, “after he fathered Seth,” the suffix refers to Adam as the father, and אֶת marks Seth as the direct object.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive construct with a third-person masculine singular subject suffix ־וֹ.

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת שֵׁת, “after he fathered Seth,” אֶת marks the personal name שֵׁת as the direct object of הוֹלִידוֹ.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת שֵׁת (“after he fathered Seth”), אֶת marks שֵׁת as the direct object of הוֹלִידוֹ, identifying Seth as the son Adam fathered.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: the son of Adam and his wife born after Abel’s death

analysis.evidence: שְׁמֹנֶה counts מֵאֹת ‘hundreds’. The phrase שְׁמֹנֶה מֵאֹת שָׁנָה gives the eight hundred years Adam lived after he fathered Seth.
analysis.sense: eight as the multiplier of hundreds

analysis.evidence: In שְׁמֹנֶה מֵאֹת שָׁנָה, שְׁמֹנֶה counts eight units of one hundred. The phrase gives the 800 years Adam lived after fathering Seth.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: In שְׁמֹנֶה מֵאֹת שָׁנָה, the singular noun supplies the unit for the count “eight hundred years.” The phrase measures the portion of Adam’s life after he fathered Seth.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Adam is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד, and בָּנִים וּבָנוֹת (‘sons and daughters’) are its direct objects. The preceding phrase אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת שֵׁת (‘after he fathered Seth’) uses the same verb for Adam’s fatherhood.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־
